To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

long-term exposure of insulinoma INS- 1 β cells to linoleate (an unsaturated FFA) and glucose in vitro causes cell dysfunction and apoptosis through mitochondrial-mediated pathways, and increased glucose in culture medium enhances linoleate-induced β-cell dysfunction.
long-term exposure of β-cells to high linoleic acid concentrations in the presence of elevated glucose levels may cause β-cell dysfunction through mitochondrial-mediated mechanisms.
chronic exposure of INS- 1 β cells to linoleate in vitro induces cell dysfunction, apoptosis and death, which are dependent on mitochondrial-mediated signal pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mitochondrial-mediated pathways by which long-term linoleic acid exposure induces β-cell dysfunction, and may be helpful for further studies of the pathogenesis of type 2 diabetic complications.
the mechanisms of β-cell dysfunction and the potential role of linoleic acid in the development of diabetes.
the mitochondrial-mediated mechanisms of linoleic acid on the dysfunction and apoptosis of INS-1 β-cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
long-term exposure of β-cells to linoleic acids and glucose in vitro leads to cell dysfunction and death through a mitochondrial-mediated pathway.
chronic exposure to high linoleic acid levels and glucose levels induced β-cell dysfunction, which involved mitochondrial-mediated pathways.

long-term exposure of rat insulinoma cells INS-1 to high linoleic acid concentrations (500 μM) and glucose concentrations (25 mM), which are similar to those in the diabetic state, can lead to β-cell dysfunction and death, which is dependent, in part, on a mitochondrial-mediated pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
linoleic acid is toxic to β cells, especially at high glucose levels, and that the toxicity is mediated by a mitochondrial-mediated pathway.
long-term exposure to linoleate induces mitochondrial-mediated apoptosis and dysfunction in insulin-secreting β cells.
chronic exposure of INS- 1 cells to linole acid in vitro affects cell survival and function via a mitochondrial-mediated mechanism, which is enhanced by high glucose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
linoleic acid, a common FFA, can induce β-cell dysfunction through a mitochondrial-mediated signal transduction pathway and that high glucose levels enhance linoleic acid toxicity in β cells.
the mitochondrial-mediated pathway is a potential target for the treatment of type 2 diabets.

chronic exposure of INS- 1 cells to linoleate in high glucose culture medium may be a useful model to mimic the effects of excessive levels of circulating FFAs in obesity and/or diabetes on pancreatic β-cells.
